findings.where: Hero, first screen at desktop and phone
findings.fault: Mark himself is missing. There is no photograph of him, not even a labelled stand-in, and nothing in his own voice. The first screen is the mark, a red name in capitals, one line in the third person and a button. The visitor is asked to write to someone they cannot see or hear.
findings.who_objects: The development-bank official, who is choosing an individual advisor and wants to see the person before writing to them. Mark also objects: the brief's client value 3 ('the man himself') must hold in every direction, and first-visit trust item 1 requires a real photo for a solo practice.

findings.where: Nav lockup (the small mark and 'MMM INFRA') and the large hero aqueduct
findings.fault: The logo is recoloured. The arches are drawn in the palette's 'cut' near-black instead of the logo grey #404040, and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark is dark instead of logo blue #0070C0. Mark has not opened the logo colours.
findings.who_objects: Mark, whose recognisable blue wordmark disappears from his own site, and visitors who know the mark from his LinkedIn or earlier work. The house rule 'never recolour a logo' bars it, and the brief says the mark is never redrawn.

findings.where: Hero name heading, article heading, 'CINZEL' specimen and the 'LAID · WEIGHTY · SETTLED' heading, against the 'WRITE TO MARK' button
findings.fault: Minium red is meant to mark the one action, but every heading uses it too. The 64 px red name easily outweighs the small red button. Red therefore marks no single function, and the action is not the strongest thing on the screen.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who takes in a page of red capitals and has to look for the action instead of being led to it. The function walk reserves the primary action's colour, and the visual-weight order (name first, button a distant second) does not match the task order.

findings.fault: The tabula ansata 'ears' are separate triangles floating clear of the red block. Instead of reading as one dovetailed tablet, they read as two arrowheads pointing in at the label, like a carousel or a bow. The gap breaks closure, so the button looks like three objects.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who is unsure whether the triangles are separate controls (back and forward arrows) and who reads the shape as gimmicky rather than as the measured look of a senior lawyer.

findings.where: Pull quote in the article specimen, against the 'WRITE TO MARK' button
findings.fault: The static pull quote has the button's shape: an edged box with dovetail ears on both sides. It uses dark instead of red, but one look now means both 'press this' and 'a quotation'. The parts map flags it as looking actable.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article, who may click the quote expecting it to act. This is a function-walk fault (each look must mean one function). The direction card asks for the ansata as both button and pull quote, so it is a clash to put to the founder.

findings.fault: The 'AA' swatch is a filled minium block with light capitals in the button's colour and type. It looks like a second, unlabelled red button. The parts map flags it as looking actable.
findings.who_objects: The visitor, who sees two red filled boxes with capital labels and wonders which one acts. It also undercuts the tile's own claim that minium is 'the one action'.

findings.fault: A button that replays the animation looks like a link: underlined spaced capitals with no fill or edge. It takes the link's reserved underline, and its look matches the article's underlined link, which navigates.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reviewing the tile (Mark, Angélique), who cannot tell whether clicking it replays the animation in place or leaves the page.

findings.where: Contact route across the page (the hero button, the nav 'CONTACT' link and the missing footer)
findings.fault: The only way to make contact is a mailto button. The email address never appears as text, and there is no footer with it. On a managed office machine where mailto opens nothing or the wrong client, the visitor has no address to copy.
findings.who_objects: The bank official working on a locked-down corporate desktop, who needs the address to paste into Outlook or forward to procurement. First-visit trust item 7 asks for the full address as its own link text.

findings.where: Hero subline, and the absence of anything after it on the first screen
findings.fault: The one credential line is the only proof. Nothing shows the regions Mark has worked in, where he is based, or his newest article or talk. The visitor learns what he was, not what he does now or where.
findings.who_objects: The procurement-minded official, who judges an advisor by project kind and region (first-visit trust items 3, 6 and 13, and 'Feel the CV'), and who cannot tell from this screen whether he covers their region.

findings.where: Article specimen heading ('THE WORLD'S BEST PUBLIC-PRIVATE PARTNERSHIP LAW'), and the type-pair rule 'Headings … always in capitals'
findings.fault: All headings must be tracked Cinzel capitals, so a moderately long title already runs to three shouting lines. Mark's real titles are longer ('Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge'), and in capitals they become a slow block to read. Every new post Angélique adds will inherit this.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning Mark's articles for one on their topic, and Angélique, whose new posts will look worse the longer their titles are (client value 9).

findings.fault: Interpuncts part every word, so 'INFRASTRUCTURE · ADVISOR' reads as two separate items rather than one job title, and 'M' stands alone like a word. On phone the dot between them drops when the line wraps, so the treatment is not consistent across widths.
findings.who_objects: A first-time visitor, who reads the heading as a list and takes a beat to parse it as 'Mark M Moseley, infrastructure advisor'.

findings.where: Motion sketch notes (the 'cubic-bezier(…)' code and '#13, docs/research/animation-length.md F5/F12'), and the palette notes
findings.fault: Internal ticket numbers, a repo file path and CSS code appear in the candidate's own text. The code is set in a default monospace that is larger and heavier than the Alegreya around it, so it breaks the type pair the tile is meant to show.
findings.who_objects: Mark, reviewing the direction, who meets developer jargon and a stray third typeface in a tile meant to show him one look.

findings.where: Article specimen meta line on phone ('MMM INFRA BLOG NO. 8 · 18 SEPTEMBER / 2024')
findings.fault: At 390 px the date breaks across lines and leaves the year alone on the second line.
findings.who_objects: A phone reader, who sees a ragged, unfinished-looking date under every article heading.

findings.where: 'STAND-IN' label in the texture tile, and the empty 'GRANITE' swatch
findings.fault: The stand-in label is outlined spaced capitals in a box, which is the look of a small outlined button. The granite swatch is an empty edged box that reads as an empty input field.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reviewing the tile, who may try to click the label or wonder what the blank box is for. Both are flagged in the parts map as looking actable.
